races.name: Discover Newmarket Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Racing Welfare Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Livemore
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with one start behind him (5th over 8f, Good), so the extra furlong here is a query; Connor Planas takes the ride for T J Kent, who has been out of form over 14 days (0/5), and 47 days off adds a fitness dimension.|

runners_data.name: Parc Dosne
runners_data.note: Two runs at 10f on Good and Soft suggest stamina is not a problem stepping back to a mile, but both outings ended in mid-pack finishes without winning; Mason Paetel's 5lb claim is a marginal help, though Matt Crawley's 14-day record (0/1) is thin.|

runners_data.name: Vastern
runners_data.note: Lightly raced — one outing only, finishing second over 7f on Good — which leaves plenty unknown but the step to a mile with Pat Cosgrave in the plate for Adam Kirby is a logical progression; his unknown style tag means his positioning on race day is an open question, making him a tactical wildcard.|

runners_data.name: Anncanya
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed — no form string and no days-since-last-run recorded — so David Probert and Peter Chapple-Hyam are operating in the dark here; going is listed UNKNOWN for this runner, and the lightly raced flag means nothing can be taken for granted either way.|

runners_data.name: La Mariposa
runners_data.note: Placed 8th and 5th in her two runs, both on ground softer than today, for the Charalambous & Clutterbuck yard; a natural hold-up horse by preference, she is shown in midfield on the map because the rear ranks are congested, and the style mismatch tempers confidence even if the Good going is within her compass.|

runners_data.name: Cerro Blanco
runners_data.note: The race's lone pace-setter, with a win and a runner-up at Newmarket over 7f for Charlie Appleby — an elite yard firing at 6/22 over 14 days; stepping up to a mile is the one open question, but his uncontested lead is the dominant tactical asset in this field regardless of that step-up.|

runners_data.name: El Carrusel
runners_data.note: A 253-day absence is the standout concern, and his five-run form string (7-4-7-2-6) reveals inconsistency; Donagh Murphy's 7lb claim is a positive, but as a natural hold-up type pushed into a midfield mapping due to field congestion, he faces both a positioning problem and a fitness question after nearly nine months away.|

races.paceDynamic: Cerro Blanco is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press him from the outset, Billy Loughnane should be able to dictate from the front at a controlled, measured tempo over this mile. The remaining six runners are all hold-up or unknown-style types, meaning the pace will be set entirely on Cerro Blanco's terms — a steady gallop that compresses the field and limits the premium on finishing kick. The field does, however, hold more hold-up horses than can naturally settle at the rear; La Mariposa and El Carrusel are genuine closers by preference but are shown in midfield because the rear ranks are crowded, and neither is assured of finding their natural position. This race shape strongly favours a horse capable of tracking the leader from a prominent pitch and sustaining the effort through the final two furlongs, or Cerro Blanco himself if he can convert his lead into a controlled solo display.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cerro Blanco Controls Solo
scenarios.trigger: If Cerro Blanco dictates an uncontested pace and his rivals fail to close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: Loughnane settles Cerro Blanco in front at a comfortable gallop, denying hold-up horses the strong pace they need to generate momentum, and the Appleby colt's class advantage over lower-rated rivals tells in the final furlong. The controlled tempo means closers never find the sustained gallop to reel him in, and his course-distance form (1st, 2nd both at Newmarket) underlines his suitability.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Picks Up Late
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent tracker sits just off Cerro Blanco and produces a stronger finish through the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A horse like Vastern or Anncanya settles second or third, conserves energy in the compressed mid-race pace, and produces the decisive kick as Cerro Blanco ties up inside the final furlong. The moderate tempo keeps the race together long enough for a well-positioned hold-up type to swoop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently in the final three furlongs to create genuine late-closing opportunity for the rear-rank runners.
scenarios.body: La Mariposa or Livemore, tracking from further back than ideal, benefits from a late injection of pace that stretches the field and allows them to pick off tired rivals inside the final furlong. This scenario requires Cerro Blanco to have gone too hard earlier, which is against the grain of his one confirmed front-running profile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank Outsider Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at such a muddling tempo that a complete surprise package like El Carrusel gets a soft lead-and-coast scenario by accident.
scenarios.body: El Carrusel, having been off 253 days and dropped to a low OR, stumbles into an unexpectedly soft piece of running, but his lengthy absence and poor recent form figures make this a remote outcome. The scenario requires multiple things to go wrong simultaneously and carries very little evidential support.

watchPoints.text: Cerro Blanco's absence of 77 days combined with the step from 7f to 1m means watch his sectionals in the early stages — if Loughnane has to work harder than expected to lead, his stamina reserves could be compromised.|

La Mariposa and El Carrusel are both natural hold-up horses likely to race out of their preferred positions; watch whether either can manoeuvre to the rear once the gates open, as their chance depends heavily on finding genuine space they may not get.|

Vastern and Anncanya are both lightly raced unknowns — watch the market move and paddock behaviour closely, as either trainer could be sitting on significantly more ability than one run (or no run) has revealed.|

With a lone front-runner setting an uncontested pace, watch whether the field concertinas behind Cerro Blanco in the early stages — if the entire field is within two lengths entering the final two furlongs, the race becomes a sprint finish that suits a horse with the sharpest turn of foot rather than the best stamina.|

races.name: Racing TV Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Patrol
runners_data.note: Trainer Dylan Cunha sends out a 4-year-old who has placed at 1m2f on good going but is stepping to 1m4f in a race it is expected to lead; the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that it is somewhat out of role as a natural prominent horse now used as pace-setter, which slightly tempers its win chance, though the small field mitigates that concern.|
runners_data.comment: Patrol has been runner-up twice in his last five starts, including two starts back, but remains without a win after a fair fourth last time out. The eye-catching stat is our rating of 99, some 21 pounds above his modest official mark of 78, making him a clear standout on our figures in this smaller field.

runners_data.name: Level Look
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 3-year-old is trained by a handler firing at 20% over 14 days and has a smart win to its name over 1m2f at Sandown, but 189 days off is a serious fitness question mark at a trip it has not yet been asked to handle over a mile and four furlongs.|
runners_data.comment: Level Look won last time out, the pick of a spell that also included a fourth and an unplaced run before it, but that was 189 days ago and he returns fresh. The lengthy absence is the obvious question for a gelding who leaves the form boost of that latest success in his favour.

runners_data.name: Cranachan
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's hold-up type has won over 1m2f on good going and placed twice in similar conditions, making it the most course-and-distance-suited closer in the field; the hood is noted, Hector Crouch takes over, and 27 days since its last run leaves it likely cherry-ripe.|
runners_data.comment: Cranachan won two starts back, was a close second three starts back, and only managed fourth last time out. The yard is firing too, landing 30% of runners in the last fortnight, and fit 27 days on, he's a leading threat here.

runners_data.name: Counter Intuitive
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's 3-year-old won impressively over 1m2f on good going last time and Billy Loughnane, riding at a yard operating at 18% in the 14-day window, will likely track Patrol closely and use that proximity if the front-runner weakens late.|
runners_data.comment: Counter Intuitive won last time out, a big step up on the two starts before that when only sixth and eighth. Fit 31 days on and with today's trip in her favour, she's the type who can build on that new-found form, though there's little proven depth to her figure yet.

races.paceDynamic: Patrol is the sole confirmed front-runner in this four-runner field over a mile and four furlongs, and with Counter Intuitive also holding prominent tendencies, there is at least one horse to push forward alongside or just behind Patrol into the early stages. However, in such a small field, Patrol is unlikely to be seriously pressured and should control the tempo at a sustainable, measured gallop — classic small-field conditions where the pace is honest but not searching. Level Look and Cranachan are both hold-up types who will track off the pace and rely on the race developing into a stamina test or a meaningful late surge. The race shape strongly favours hold-up or close-tracking horses that can sustain a run off a steady gallop — provided the tempo is genuine enough to stop Patrol or Counter Intuitive simply stealing it from the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Patrol controls a modest tempo unchallenged and the hold-up horses cannot generate enough momentum from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Patrol settles in front at a comfortable gallop across 1m4f, with no genuine pressure to stretch its stamina, and the race is essentially won before the final two furlongs; Counter Intuitive, tracking closely, also benefits from the proximity premium in this small field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to drain Patrol's reserves and the closers sweep past in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Cranachan and Level Look, both sitting off the pace, get the strong gallop they need to deliver a late run that punishes any front-runner who has overextended; Cranachan's solid form at this trip on good ground gives it the best credentials among the pair to finish powerfully.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Counter Intuitive Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Counter Intuitive tracks Patrol closely and is sent for home early by Loughnane, exploiting the gap before the closers engage.
scenarios.body: Counter Intuitive, who won over 1m2f on good going last time, takes advantage of Patrol's potential fatigue by kicking on turning in; with only three rivals to beat and an in-form partnership behind it, a prominent position here is a significant tactical asset.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Pair Collide
scenarios.trigger: If Level Look, returning after 189 days, lacks the race fitness to sustain its run while Cranachan also finds the pace too modest to suit its closing style.
scenarios.body: A muddled finish ensues where no single horse lands a telling blow in the straight, leaving the race open to a fortunate position from whichever horse is closest to the pace at the two-furlong pole.

watchPoints.text: Watch Patrol's early tempo — if it sets an uncontested crawl through the early furlongs, Level Look and Cranachan may lack the necessary pace injection to reel in the leader, making the front-runners very hard to peg back.

Level Look's 189-day absence is a significant concern; watch for any signs of greenness or sluggishness in the paddock or early on course that could confirm it needs this run as a fitness exercise rather than a genuine winning attempt.

Cranachan's hood and the jockey change to Hector Crouch are worth monitoring — if the headgear signals any temperament concern, it could disrupt the horse's ability to settle cleanly and deliver its usual finish.

With only four runners, gaps in the field could open up earlier than usual turning into the Newmarket straight, so watch which jockey commits first — Counter Intuitive's Loughnane is likely to make an aggressive move if he spots daylight at the two-furlong pole.

races.name: National Stud Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: High Degree
runners_data.note: William Haggas's charge has course form and a good record on similar going (7 runs, 1W 5P), but is stepping up to 1m2f from recent 8-9f starts and is technically racing as a front-runner today despite a prominent style tag — his ability to control the pace is his primary asset, and that may be enough on a flat track over a trip slightly beyond his recent comfort zone.|
runners_data.comment: High Degree is winless in his last five starts but ran a clear second three starts back, and a fifth last time doesn't dent his claim as our top-rated runner. Fit 17 days on and proven over today's trip from stall 6, he's the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Al Aali
runners_data.note: George Scott's gelding has been beaten out of sight on five consecutive attempts over 10-12f on good ground (0W 0P from 7 sim-going runs), wears a bit and arrives just 13 days after his last run — the hold-up style is genuine but the form profile on this surface and trip raises serious questions.|
runners_data.comment: Al Aali is winless in his last six starts, no better than fifth in that time, but sits ten pounds clear of his official mark of 88 on our rating of 98. Fit 13 days on and race-proven over today's trip, the worry is whether that below-par recent form can turn round.

runners_data.name: Way Of Life
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old veteran who has won three of his last five starts, though all three wins came on Standard AW at Southwell, and his only Good turf run in the last five was a fifth over 12f — Olivia Tubb's 5lb claim helps, but the jump back to turf on Good going after 81 days off is the key query here.|
runners_data.comment: Way Of Life won last time out, one of three wins in his last five starts, but he's had 81 days off since and returns fresh. Proven over today's trip, the layoff is the obvious question for a leading contender.

runners_data.name: Percy's Daydream
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old is in excellent form (4W 8P from 13 sim-going runs) and has won over both 10f and 12f on Good ground recently — though the runner list shows him mapped to midfield, his natural instinct is to race prominently, and David Probert will likely push him forward from the outset.|
runners_data.comment: Percy's Daydream won two starts back, one of two victories in her last five starts, despite a below-par fourth last time out. The yard is out of form though, managing only 4% winners in the last fortnight, a concern for a filly otherwise proven over today's trip.

runners_data.name: War Hawk
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford's gelding returns from a 126-day absence in tongue-tie and has a solid 12f record on Good Newmarket turf — like Percy's Daydream, his true style is prominent rather than the midfield position the crowded map assigns him, and apprentice Mason Paetel's 5lb claim slightly offsets the fitness concern.|
runners_data.comment: War Hawk is winless in his last five starts and was well held in fifth last time out, his only real form coming five starts back when second. A 126-day absence adds to the questions, though he arrives with experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Darn Hot Gallop
runners_data.note: James Tate's lightly-raced three-year-old won back-to-back races over 7-8f earlier in the season but has disappointed in three subsequent starts on Good turf, and today represents a significant step up to 1m2f — his front-running instincts are genuine, but the combination of trip, regression in form, and a competitive handicap mark makes this a tough assignment.|
runners_data.comment: Darn Hot Gallop strung together three straight wins but has been unplaced in each of her last two starts, a downturn that makes her hard to fancy on our figures here. She is fresh enough though, having last run 28 days ago.

races.paceDynamic: High Degree is the sole confirmed front-runner here and should be able to dictate from the front on his own terms with no genuine rival prepared to take him on for the lead — a controlled, sustainable gallop is the likely outcome rather than a searingly true-run test. Way Of Life and Percy's Daydream are the most natural stalkers and should slot in just behind, while War Hawk, Percy's Daydream, and Darn Hot Gallop are all true prominent types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because five horses cannot simultaneously occupy the front two positions — of those, Percy's Daydream and Darn Hot Gallop are most likely to actually push forward given their recent front-running form, which could inject more pressure on High Degree than the map implies. Al Aali is the only genuine hold-up horse in a field that is overwhelmingly front-end and prominent in character, meaning any late closer faces the task of picking off rivals who are collectively bunched ahead of them. With one pace-setter dictating a fair but uncontested gallop over 1m2f on good ground, this race shape decisively favours horses that can sit just off the leader in a prominent or tracking position and sustain their effort through the straight, rather than deep hold-up horses or those forced to race genuinely out of role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: High Degree Dictates Steadily
scenarios.trigger: If High Degree sets a controlled, uncontested pace and the field strings out behind without significant challenge.
scenarios.body: High Degree leads at his own tempo, sapping the finishing kick from hold-up horses, while those who track closest get first run in the straight; prominent trackers Way Of Life and Percy's Daydream are ideally placed to pounce as the pace is not strong enough to set up a late challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Bunching Causes Scrimmage
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent horses — Percy's Daydream, War Hawk, Darn Hot Gallop — all push forward early and crowd the pace, injecting a more genuine gallop.
scenarios.body: The early crowding lifts the tempo beyond what High Degree wants, and a truer-run race opens the door for those who settle just off a competitive pace; War Hawk, fresh from a 126-day break but course-fit on good ground, benefits from a stronger test at this trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Denied By Modest Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and the field idles together, compressing the finish into a sprint from 2f out.
scenarios.body: A slowly-run 1m2f becomes a tactical lottery, favouring the horse with the best turn of foot from a tracking position rather than any deep hold-up runner; Al Aali, the only true hold-up horse, is disadvantaged as there is no genuine pace to close into.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unexposed Type Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to soften the leaders and a hold-up or midfield horse delivers a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Al Aali would need a strongly-run race to land this from the rear, but his sim-going figures show zero wins and zero places from seven attempts on good ground, making this a genuinely low-probability shape; Darn Hot Gallop stepping back from the front would be the more credible beneficiary of any late fade by the leaders.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Percy's Daydream, Darn Hot Gallop, or War Hawk push aggressively forward at the start — if two or more of these naturally prominent horses challenge High Degree for the early lead, the pace dynamic shifts materially and the controlled scenario collapses.

Way Of Life's turf form on Good going is thin (one place from three turf runs in the last five), and if the ground is riding firmer than expected the switch back from Southwell AW could catch him out at a crucial moment.

War Hawk's 126-day absence is a significant fitness flag — if Simon & Ed Crisford have not specifically prepared him for a first-time win off a layoff, he may find the closing stages beyond him regardless of how the race is run.

Al Aali has zero wins and zero places from seven runs on Good or similar going — punters should note this is not simply a hold-up horse waiting to pounce; the going record is a structural concern, not just a form blip.

High Degree's jockey Cieren Fallon will be crucial in managing the tempo — if he allows an overly slow pace through the first half-mile, the race could compress into a sprint finish that partially negates the advantage of leading from the front.

races.name: Madness Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Rocking Ends
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter here; Tom Clover's six-year-old has course-and-distance form on similar going (13 of 15 qualifying runs on good) and Fallon in the saddle is a key positive, though the STYLE_FIT tag signals it is racing somewhat out of typical role and should be assessed accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Rocking Ends is winless in his last six starts and was below par when seventh last time, though he'd shown much better before that. Quick to return just 7 days on and proven over today's trip, he heads this contest on our figures as top-rated.

runners_data.name: Valley Ofthe Kings
runners_data.note: Drops to 5f from a string of 6f and 7f runs, which is a query over this minimum trip, and Dylan Cunha's yard is out of form (0/13 in 14 days); prominent style suits the pace shape but the step down in trip and trainer form tempers enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Valley Ofthe Kings was a good second last time out and also placed second five starts back, either side of three below-par efforts. Without a win in that spell, he returns 27 days on with today's trip already navigated, making him a leading threat on our figures.

runners_data.name: Grandlad
runners_data.note: Returned from 82 days off to win on good ground over 5f last time out, which is the standout recent form line in this field; holds-up by style but has the course-and-distance winning evidence to arrive late if a genuine gallop develops.
runners_data.comment: Grandlad won last time out, his only success in his last five starts, but he's had 82 days off since and returns fresh. Proven over today's trip, the long layoff is the obvious question for this leading contender.

runners_data.name: Rogue Bullet
runners_data.note: A naturally prominent racer whose 5f form on good ground is solid (four finishes in the first five at this trip and going type); James Owen's yard in strong 14-day form (8/48) and Billy Loughnane a major positive — well positioned to exploit any weakness in the leader late.
runners_data.comment: Rogue Bullet won two starts back but has since dipped, finishing fourth last time out after modest form either side of that success. Fit again 20 days on and with today's trip already navigated, he sits respectably on our figures without being fluent on recent evidence.

runners_data.name: Diomed Duke
runners_data.note: True hold-up type with a fair record on good ground at 5f (9 of 13 qualifying runs) but career form has been inconsistent; Stuart Williams yard ticking over at 3/21 in 14 days, and at OR 72 has the lowest ceiling bar the two below him — needs a lot to go right from the back.
runners_data.comment: Diomed Duke is winless in his last five starts and was well held in fifth last time out, though a third three starts back shows more within him. Fit 27 days on and proven over today's trip, our rating of 81 sits well above his official mark of 72.

runners_data.name: Tuscan Point
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer by style but redistributed to midfield here because the rear is oversubscribed; form figures include a win and a placed effort in good going but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) means it is unlikely to get its preferred position — Adam Kirby training without a recent winner (0/16, 14 days).
runners_data.comment: Tuscan Point was well beaten when unplaced last time out, well below the level of a win and a couple of runner-up efforts earlier in that spell. Race-fit 11 days on and with today's trip in his favour, he's still rated among the least of this field on our figures.

runners_data.name: Travel Agent
runners_data.note: Won twice this season including over 6f on good-ish surfaces, but true hold-up style is compromised by the crowded rear — shown in midfield for mapping purposes rather than by natural inclination; the step back to 5f is untested at this level, and Kirby's yard in the same cold streak (0/16) is an additional concern.
runners_data.comment: Travel Agent strung together back-to-back wins earlier in his last six starts, but the form has since tailed off to a seventh last time out. Fit 15 days on and with today's trip in his favour, the recent drop-off leaves him the least fancied of this field on our figures.

runners_data.name: Ecclefechan
runners_data.note: John Ryan's three-year-old has the lowest OR in the field and a recent form string that reads 554986 — no win and no placed effort in the last six; a true hold-up type pushed into midfield on the map by distribution, and the youngest, lightest-weighted runner facing older rivals with more 5f experience.
runners_data.comment: Ecclefechan is winless in his last six starts, with his best a fourth-placed effort four starts back and nothing better last time out. Quick to return just 8 days on and with today's trip in his favour, there's little here to inspire real confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Rocking Ends is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 5f handicap and, with no other genuine pace horse to challenge for the lead, Cieren Fallon can dictate terms from the front at a controlled, sustainable tempo. Valley Ofthe Kings and Rogue Bullet are the next most likely to press from prominent positions, but neither is a natural leader, meaning Rocking Ends should enjoy a comfortable, uncontested rail or near-rail berth through the early furlongs. The field contains a significant cluster of true hold-up horses — Tuscan Point, Travel Agent, and Ecclefechan — who are all mapped to midfield because there is simply no room for all of them to operate from their natural rear position; of those three, Tuscan Point's recent form and early pace suggest they are most likely to drift toward midfield rather than the back. This race shape heavily favours front-running and prominent-racing profiles: a lone, unfussed pace-setter over a sharp 5f on good turf sets up a race where those who race close to the action are best placed to pounce, while genuine hold-up horses face a structurally compromised scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rocking Ends Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Rocking Ends is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a measured, honest gallop through the first two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Fallon dictates the fractions on the front end and the field spreads out behind without ever truly pressuring him, leaving Rocking Ends with energy in reserve to repel challengers at the furlong pole; prominent racers who track him closely are best positioned to inherit the prize if he ties up, but he has the class and course-form profile to see it out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Rocking Ends goes too fast early or tightens up inside the final furlong, allowing a close-tracking prominent horse to sweep past.
scenarios.body: A contested or slightly hot pace — even self-inflicted — sees Rocking Ends flatten out and the horses racing just off his shoulder in the slipstream get the perfect tow into the race; Rogue Bullet and Valley Ofthe Kings are ideally positioned by style to capitalise on any late weakness from the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the field strings out, creating a true end-to-end gallop that leaves a late gap on the stands side or rail.
scenarios.body: Grandlad, who has proven course-and-distance form including a recent win on good ground, is best equipped among the deeper-drawn runners to pick up late if a genuine run of racing unfolds; Diomed Duke is also capable of finishing off races on this ground type but needs everything to fall right.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compressed Finish, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If traffic is tight throughout, the pace collapses late, and the field bunches in the final furlong creating a blanket finish.
scenarios.body: In a bunched scenario on a flat 5f track the widest spread of finishing positions compresses and any horse racing in a pocket faces elimination; this benefits Rocking Ends or a horse lucky enough to find a clear passage, but this shape is low probability given the lack of genuine pace pressure.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Valley Ofthe Kings's handlers opt for any forcing tactics to compensate for the step to minimum trip — if they do, it could unexpectedly pressure Rocking Ends and collapse the expected controlled pace scenario.

Grandlad's 82-day absence before his last win is a form-freshness flag worth monitoring in the paddock; if he shows signs of a forward, well-schooled preparation he becomes significantly more dangerous to the pace scenario.

Tuscan Point, Travel Agent, and Ecclefechan are all genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield — watch how they break from the gates, as any one of them attempting to race forward could create early crowding and disrupt the field's natural order.

Billy Loughnane on Rogue Bullet is worth tracking given the trainer's hot 14-day strike rate (8/48) — if Rogue Bullet gets a clean passage just off the pace it is precisely the horse built to profit if Rocking Ends fades late.

Rocking Ends carries a visor (hg:v) which can sharpen focus and early speed — monitor how quickly Fallon moves to take his lead position from the stalls, as an aggressive break would cement the race shape described in Scenario A.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Rose Of Honour
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in her last three starts all at 6f, including two on standard Tapeta, and her one run on good turf produced a win; James Tate's stable is 1/14 in a 14-day window but she is the confirmed pace-setter here and her ability to control tempo uncontested is her single biggest asset, though she races as a prominent type rather than a pure tearaway front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Rose Of Honour won three in a row before an unplaced effort last time out, the obvious blip in an otherwise flawless spell. Proven over today's trip and fit again 27 days on, she's the clear form standout and the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Novamay
runners_data.note: Rhys Elliott (5lb claimer) takes the ride and she has a recent win at 6f on soft, but her record on good going reads 5th-9th in two outings from 13 handicap runs on that surface; she is a natural prominent racer but with Elara May, Lady Kodiac, and Rose Of Honour all wanting early positions, she is likely to find herself shuffled into midfield, a role that doesn't play to her strengths.
runners_data.comment: Novamay won last time out, a bright end to an otherwise modest run of finishes no better than fourth before that. Fit again 27 days on and with today's trip in her favour, she has claims but needs to prove that improvement wasn't a one-off.

runners_data.name: Elara May
runners_data.note: A 259-day absence is the headline concern, but Philip McBride has managed her lightly throughout her career and she has winning form at 5f-6f on both good and soft — her return from a long break should not be automatically dismissed; races prominently, which is exactly the profile the race shape favours, and Pat Cosgrave is a sharp judge of pace at Newmarket.
runners_data.comment: Elara May won three of her last five starts, including back-to-back victories four and five starts back, and was a solid fourth last time out. She has been off the track for 259 days since, though, and that lengthy absence is the obvious question for a filly proven over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Angel Shared
runners_data.note: Dougie Costello partners a mare who has shown ability at 5f-6f on good ground (three wins at those trips) but her recent form string of 7-5-3-13-6 shows inconsistency; a hold-up runner who needs things to fall right late, and with pace likely to be controlled rather than frantic, she faces an uphill task generating the momentum she needs over 6f.
runners_data.comment: Angel Shared is winless in her last five starts, below par in sixth last time out, though a third three starts back hints at more. Our rating of 89 sits well above her mark of 81, and with today's trip already navigated, that gap makes her a threat 21 days on.

runners_data.name: Lady Kodiac
runners_data.note: Twice placed at 6f on good ground and the winner of a 6f Tapeta race, she is a James Tate second string in this race; a prominent racer who should comfortably secure a forward berth in a field where midfield is congested, and her 2-2 record at 6f on good/standard surfaces suggests the trip and conditions suit.
runners_data.comment: Lady Kodiac was a solid second last time out, one of two placed efforts since a win five starts back, and our rating of 92 sits well clear of her official mark of 85. Fit 29 days on and proven over today's trip, she's a leading threat in this field.

runners_data.name: Powdering
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane partners a 6-year-old who most recently won over this exact course and distance on good going — the strongest form pointer in her locker and a key stat; her hold-up style means she requires the front to have set a strong enough tempo to come back to her in the straight, and her wider record on good ground (1 win from 15 runs) is a sobering qualifier.
runners_data.comment: Powdering won last time out but that followed a mixed spell including two unplaced efforts and a modest sixth, and she's only our seventh-rated runner in an admittedly deep field. Fit 21 days on and with today's trip in her favour, the latest success is the one thing to cling to.

runners_data.name: Shallow
runners_data.note: Six days since her last run is sharp enough to flag as a potential staleness or fitness question, and she wears a visor; recent form of 2-3-3 in 6f good-ground races is solid and consistent, but she is a hold-up horse whose true position is off the back, and in a race where pace is controlled, she may not get the strong gallop needed to make her late run effective — the style-fit discount applies.
runners_data.comment: Shallow is winless in her last six starts and was well beaten in ninth last time out, though that followed a much better run of seconds and thirds. Quick back into action just 6 days on, our rating of 84 still sits above her official mark of 78 despite that flat finish.

runners_data.name: Sing The Blues
runners_data.note: 251 days off the track is a significant concern for a 3-year-old trained by Martin Dunne, who sends just one runner over a 14-day window; a natural front-running or prominent type, she is likely to be outpaced for position and will find herself racing in midfield contrary to her preferred role, making her a speculative proposition on return from such a lengthy absence.
runners_data.comment: Sing The Blues was pulled up last time out, a worrying end to a spell that had otherwise included a win two starts back, and she has been off the track for 251 days since. Rated the field's outsider on our figures, the big absence and that below-par finish leave plenty to prove.

races.paceDynamic: Rose Of Honour is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no one likely to seriously press her from the off, she should be able to control tempo from the front on her own terms over this 6f Newmarket straight. The redistribution of Novamay, Sing The Blues, and Shallow tells the real story: this field is packed with horses that want to race prominently or close to the pace, meaning those three are unlikely to secure their natural positions and will race in a more compressed midfield group than they'd prefer. Elara May and Lady Kodiac are genuine prominent types who will push forward behind Rose Of Honour, creating a well-strung-out early order rather than a dawdle. The tactical verdict is clear: horses that can race handily or just off a sustainable, controlled pace — tracking the leader at two or three lengths — are best placed to pounce in the final two furlongs, making the prominent-to-midfield profile the dominant winning shape in this race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Rose Of Honour dictates a true but manageable pace and clears the field before the dip.
scenarios.body: Rose Of Honour has won twice at 6f on good ground and loves to bowl along at the head of affairs; unchallenged, she can dictate a rhythm that suits her stamina and sprint combination, making her very hard to reel in. Prominent trackers Elara May and Lady Kodiac are the primary threats if she is to be collared late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Rose Of Honour's early pace is just lively enough to soften her up, allowing a close-tracking second or third to wear her down.
scenarios.body: Elara May has winning form at 6f on good ground and is proven off a strong gallop, and Lady Kodiac's two placed efforts at 6f suggest she travels well close to the pace before finishing off; either can profit from a fractional fade by the leader in the final furlong. This shape heavily suits the genuine prominent types who secure a position just behind Rose Of Honour through the first three furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If pace proves strong enough to compromise the front two and give genuine hold-up horses a late winning run.
scenarios.body: Powdering showed a 1-win-from-15 record on good ground which tempers confidence, but her most recent form includes a win over this exact course and distance on good going; Shallow's form figures of 2-3-3 in recent 6f good-ground races show consistency, though she is a redistributed hold-up type racing further forward than ideal. Both need a genuine end-to-end gallop, which only materialises if Rose Of Honour sets an unusually strong pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Rose Of Honour underperforms or is slow away, causing the field to bunch and produce an unpredictable finish.
scenarios.body: With multiple prominent types competing for positions — Novamay, Sing The Blues, and Elara May all wanting to race forward — a sudden lack of confirmed pace could produce a messy, muddling race where positional advantage counts above all else. In this unlikely scenario, Angel Shared's hold-up style with a late burst or an opportunist like Novamay, if she gets her natural position back, could capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Rose Of Honour has won three on the bounce and faces no genuine pace rival — watch whether she controls tempo so well that she proves impossible to reel in before the dip, as her sectional fractions will dictate the outcome of every other scenario.

Novamay, Sing The Blues, and Elara May will all want to race forward simultaneously — watch the early stages for scrimmaging and crowding, as any of them losing their position could compromise their race entirely given they are not natural midfield horses.

Elara May's 259-day absence is the key unknown — watch how she loads and travels in the early stages, as a fresh horse on good Newmarket ground over 6f can be dangerous if she returns in form, but a rough reappearance would immediately discount her.

Powdering's recent course-and-distance win on good going is the form line most relevant to this surface and trip — watch whether Billy Loughnane can engineer a position closer than her usual hold-up berth, as that would significantly increase her chance of finishing powerfully.

Shallow runs six days after her last start wearing a visor — watch whether her compact turnaround leaves her short of her best, as her form is consistent but her hold-up style in a pace-controlled race makes timing everything.

races.name: Burwell Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Born A Rebel
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse operating in her natural role here; two of her last five runs at 7f on Good have resulted in a win and a place, and jockey Arron D'Arcy's 7lb claim is a useful asset, though trainer Patrick Owens is 0-from-3 in the last 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Born A Rebel has been in the shake-up recently, second last time out and again earlier on, and she already has experience over today's trip. A 27-day gap since that latest second is the only concern, but her pattern makes her a leading player here.

runners_data.name: Alafdhal
runners_data.note: All five recent runs have come at 5f-6f on Stanwick or Soft, so this 7f on Good is both a trip and going stretch; though mapped to midfield, this is a true hold-up horse whose redistribution onto unfamiliar ground and a longer trip substantially limits appeal.
runners_data.comment: Alafdhal is yet to figure in his last five starts, never finishing better than fifth, though he does have experience over today's trip. His speed figure reads sharper than his rating suggests, but ranked fifth of seven here, he needs more to trouble this field.

runners_data.name: Sedgemoor
runners_data.note: Wears headgear (p) and holds a lone course placing at 3rd/6f/GOO, but two recent runs at 7f have produced 9th and 15th — a true closer operating in a compressed midfield role here, and those 7f form figures are deeply uninspiring regardless of scenario.
runners_data.comment: Sedgemoor's figures work him a few pounds above his current official mark, and this six-race sequence includes a win to his name. He was only 9th when last seen 24 days ago, though, and bouncing back from that flat effort is the key test here.

runners_data.name: Chloe's Courage
runners_data.note: Returns after 176 days off and owns solid 7f Stanwick form including a win and two placed efforts, but all recent form is on Standard surfaces rather than Good turf; a natural hold-up type, and the long absence is the major concern before trusting her fresh.
runners_data.comment: Chloe's Courage is the bottom-rated runner here and returns from a 176-day absence, a gap hard to ignore. Her form does include a win and a runner-up effort earlier on, plus experience over today's trip, but she was only 9th last time and the lay-off leaves her hard to fancy fresh.

runners_data.name: Coolagh Magic
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Good most recently (1/6f/GOO) and wears headgear (t), which marks the current preparation as serious; a decade-old horse who is a genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield, and the step up to 7f from recent sprint form over 5f-6f introduces a stamina question.
runners_data.comment: Coolagh Magic won last time out, but that follows a run of modest efforts beforehand, and he's only sixth of seven on our rating for this race. He already has experience over today's trip, so a repeat of that improvement would put him in the mix.

runners_data.name: Prefer The Sister
runners_data.note: The standout form runner with OR 65, wins at 1/8f/GOO, 2/7f/GOO and 1/7f/GOO in her last five; wears headgear (ht), jockey Mason Paetel has no claim but trainer James Owen runs at a productive 8/48 over 14 days, and she is the one hold-up type most likely to push into a prominent position naturally.
runners_data.comment: Prefer The Sister won last time out and has two wins from her last six starts, form underlined by a quick nine-day turnaround and prior experience over today's trip. She's only third on our rating here, though, the one query against an in-form runner.

runners_data.name: Mister Mojito
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner and lone pace angle in this race; headgear (t) is fitted, he has eight runs on similar going producing one win and one place, but his OR of 69 and a style_fit flag suggest he may be racing slightly out of his sharpest role — his chance hinges entirely on whether an uncontested lead is enough to hold off a late challenge.
runners_data.comment: Mister Mojito heads our ratings here and has already shown he gets today's trip. He's without a win in his last five starts, though, with a modest sixth his latest effort three weeks ago, leaving current form as the query.

races.paceDynamic: Mister Mojito is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of seven and will stride to the front unchallenged from the off, setting whatever tempo suits him over this 7f trip on Good turf at Newmarket. Behind him, the remaining six runners — Born A Rebel, Prefer The Sister, Alafdhal, Sedgemoor, Chloe's Courage, and Coolagh Magic — are all natural hold-up types, meaning the early order behind the leader will be congested and tactical. This field contains more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Prefer The Sister, with the highest OR and a strong record at this course and trip, is the one most likely to push forward into a prominent position, while Alafdhal, Sedgemoor, Chloe's Courage, and Coolagh Magic are all true closers forced to race in unfamiliar midfield slots. With one uncontested pace-setter dictating a sustainable rhythm, this race strongly favours a horse able to sit just off the leader or track through the middle of the race and produce a sustained run — prominent racers who can stay close to Mister Mojito's fractions are structurally advantaged over horses stuck wide or deep in the pack.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mister Mojito Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Mister Mojito dictates an honest but manageable pace and no rival applies sustained pressure from the front, he converts his positional advantage.
scenarios.body: Mister Mojito enjoys a solo lead at whatever rhythm suits him, and with Good ground he can balance himself around the Newmarket July Course turns without being harried; the hold-up pack, forced to race out of their natural positions, arrives too late to peg back a front-runner who has never been pressured.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prefer The Sister Tracks, Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Prefer The Sister pushes forward early to sit second on the heels of Mister Mojito and has enough left to challenge over the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Prefer The Sister's form reads 423121 with two recent wins at 7f on Good, and she is clearly comfortable racing prominently — tracking the sole front-runner at a sustainable gallop hands her a dream position on a course she handles well.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Mister Mojito sets a genuinely fast pace and ties himself up in the final furlong, leaving the hold-up pack a wall of weary rivals to run through.
scenarios.body: Prefer The Sister or Born A Rebel would be best placed to benefit even in this shape, as the truly deep hold-up types like Alafdhal and Sedgemoor are racing out of their natural role and unlikely to find the gaps needed to finish fast enough from far back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively slow early and the field bunches, turning the race into a sprint finish from a tight group.
scenarios.body: In a steadily-run 7f, the horse who can quicken sharpest from the middle of the pack wins, but with most of this field being true hold-up types packed into false midfield positions, finding clean runs and room will be the determining factor.

watchPoints.text: Mister Mojito is the only front-runner in seven runners — if he faces any unexpected pressure early from Prefer The Sister pushing up, his ability to sustain the lead to the line is immediately compromised.

Prefer The Sister's 176-day absence for Chloe's Courage means market confidence or early movement on that runner in the ring would be meaningful — a yard having her fit fresh would change the hold-up dynamics significantly.

The four redistributed hold-up types (Alafdhal, Sedgemoor, Chloe's Courage, Coolagh Magic) will all be racing outside their natural position — watch for a congested midfield in the early stages as they shuffle for slots behind Mister Mojito.

Sedgemoor's two recent runs at this exact 7f trip produced 9th and 15th — if he tracks wide or gets shuffled back, his chance of producing a winning late run from a false midfield position is minimal and he may be worth opposing in any bet construction.

Born A Rebel is the only runner whose recent similar-going record shows a win (2/8f/GOO) and multiple places at the 7f-8f trip range on Good — if the pace is honest and the hold-up pack arrives in a wave, she is structurally the best-placed of the closers to finish off the race.
